demoscene.Description: Not to be confused with game demos, [Demoscene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demoscene) demos are showcases of people's programming and artistic prowess with fancy animated showcases.

examples.Description: ROMs that exist to showcase libraries, tools, or to help out developers with understanding SDK features.

netlib.ToolTip: A collection of tools and libraries to allow N64 homebrew developers to connect their games to the internet for multiplayer.

unfloader.ToolTip: A cross-platform and universal Nintendo64 flashcart ROM uploader, featuring a USB+debug library for libultra and libdragon, as well as GDB support.

intros.Description: Similar to Demoscene demos, these are typically more calling cards with greetings than full on showcases, but they can be just as technically interesting!

n64brew-gamejam2020.Description: In 2020, the N64brew Discord community hosted their first N64 homebrew game jam, with the theme **Size**. The jam featured judges David Doak, Allan Findlay, Neil Voss, Youtuber Snooplax, and N64brew user Buu342. The winner of the Jam this year was <ins>Telocation Gemini</ins>, taking home $676.26 of the $1,127.10 prize pool. Second place was tied by <ins>Kumi-Daiki Beatoff 64</ins> and <ins>Sblobber 64</ins>, third place was tied by <ins>Lunar Assault 64</ins> and <ins>The Swoop 64</ins>.

n64brew-gamejam2021.Description: The N64brew game jam returned for 2021, featuring Giles Goddard, Kaze Emanuar, LuigiBlood, and Samuel “Kaiser” Villarreal as guest judges. This year, the money was decided to be used for charity, with the winner choosing where the money would go. The theme was **Control**, and <ins>Wizard of the Board</ins> won this year, donating the prize pot of $1,254.38 to the [Rainforest Trust](https://www.rainforesttrust.org/). <ins>Mission Lost Control</ins> got second place while <ins>Voidblade</ins> got third.

n64brew-gamejam2022.Description: N64brew's game jam returned for 2022, with a **Spooky** theme. Judges this year were N64 Squid, Gerry (BehindTheCode.ca), and Buu342. The final prize pool of  $1369.65 was donated to [Child’s Play](https://childsplaycharity.org/) by the winning entry <ins>Styx</ins>. Second place was taken by <ins>Super Snooper Spookers</ins> while third place was <ins>Spirit Harvest</ins>.

n64brew-gamejam2023.Description: For the fourth year in a row, N64brew hosted a game jam. This year the theme was **Summer*, and the community voted on their favorite entries. <ins>Summer's Story</ins> got first place, the <ins>Megatextures demo</ins> got second, and <ins>Alien Sun</ins> got third. $776.76 was raised for the [Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson’s Research](https://www.michaeljfox.org/)

n64brew-gamejam2024.Description: Unlike previous years, the 2024 game jam only has one submission because it was a collaborative minigame jam. Everyone was given the same template and required to submit a minigame for the collection, similar to Pokemon Stadium's minigame Kids Club. The winner of this year's competition was <ins>Coin Rush</ins>, with <ins>SpaceWaves</ins> taking second and <ins>Hydra Harmonics</ins> taking third, all entries voted once again by the community. $1754 was raised for the [Alzheimer's Association](https://www.alz.org/).

n64brew-gamejam2025.Description: In 2025, the N64brew Game Jam returned to form, featuring Peter Lemon, Mike Ryan, and Ppcasm as guest judges. The winner this year was <ins>Junk Runner 64</ins>, donating $3340.29 to [AbleGamers](https://ablegamers.org/). Second place was <ins>Cathode Quest 64</ins> and third place was <ins>Phazer 64</ins>. The theme this year was **Repair**.

pom1999.Description: Similar to the PoM 98 competition, PoM returned once again for the year 1999. The winning ROM this year was Nacho64, who's team (Split) won the previous year.

portsclones.Description: This section contains ports and clones of other games. Most games will probably not have a direct download link as they will require you to build the games from the source code using a copy of the official game it's porting.

water.Description: Super Mario 64 hacker [Kaze Emanuar](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCuvSqzfO_LV_QzHdmEj84SQ) hosted a water competition for the N64, where competitors had to create the most realistic looking water.
